evals.prompt: Write an ad description for Meta for our dog-walking booking app. Owners stress when their usual walker cancels last minute; we have vetted backup walkers who can be booked within the hour.
evals.expected_output: Checks for .agents/product-marketing.md then .claude/product-marketing.md; if absent, suggests gtm-context without blocking. Writes two or three descriptions using Problem to Solution to Benefit, each 35 words or fewer, opening with what the product is. The last-minute cancellation pain is made vivid. Because the platform is Meta, the product and problem sit inside the first 125 characters and character counts are shown. Each description has a product, problem, solution, and benefit breakdown with a word count, then an assumptions list.
assertions: Checks for the shared product marketing context file before asking questions
Every description has 35 words or fewer
Every description names the product and category early
The cancellation problem is specific and felt, not generic
The product and problem appear within the first 125 characters
Shows product, problem, solution, benefit, word count, and character count
Does not invent statistics such as vetting numbers or response times beyond 'within the hour'
Contains no em dashes or exclamation marks

evals.prompt: Give me Google Ads descriptions for a password manager for small businesses. Headlines are already done: 'Stop sharing passwords by email' and 'Set up in 10 minutes'.
evals.expected_output: Switches to Google RSA platform mode. Writes four descriptions, each 90 characters or fewer with counts shown, compressed to keep the problem and benefit. Builds on the existing headlines rather than repeating them word for word. Each description reads well alongside either headline.
assertions: Provides four descriptions
Every description is 90 characters or fewer including spaces
Shows a character count next to each description
No description repeats either headline word for word
Each description includes a problem and a benefit
Uses no vague clichés such as 'seamless' or 'game-changing'

evals.prompt: Make this better: 'Great features. Easy to use. Our software makes your workflow better and you'll love it.' It's a scheduling tool for physiotherapy clinics that cuts no-shows with automatic SMS reminders.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the original: disjointed flow, no product identification, vague benefit, no problem. Rewrites with Problem to Solution to Benefit, opening with what the product is, twisting the knife on no-shows, explaining the SMS reminder mechanism, and ending on a concrete benefit. Any number (such as percentage of no-shows cut) is a placeholder, not invented. Offers ad-headline-maker if no headline exists.
assertions: Identifies disjointed flow, missing product identification, and vague benefit
Every rewrite has 35 words or fewer
Every rewrite opens by naming the product category (a scheduling tool for physiotherapy clinics or similar)
Mentions the automatic SMS reminder mechanism
Uses a placeholder such as [X]% instead of an invented statistic
Offers ad-headline-maker for a matching headline
